| Primary | Hit Die | Saves | Effect Value | Rec. Mod. |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Perception | d8 | PER, DEX | 10 \+ PER \+ PRO | \+1 |

Sentinels notice what others cannot. Not just danger: patterns, tells, trajectories, the half-second before an attack that most people never perceive. They are awareness made combat-ready. Investigators who read a crime scene like a conversation. Hunters who know where the target will be before the target has decided to go there. Marksmen who place shots through gaps that closed before anyone else saw them open. Hyper-aware martial artists who feel a strike arriving before the body moves to throw it.

The Sentinel's power is not simply seeing better. Their strength is understanding danger before it fully manifests. They do not react to the fight. They read it in advance, stay ahead of it, and make every enemy mistake into a consequence that lands before the enemy realizes what happened.

At their peak they become something more: the protective eye that covers everyone, the overwatch that makes the enemy question every decision they make.

**Threat Assessment** — Level 1 · Core Feature

At the start of each encounter before initiative is rolled, the GM tells you three things about the creatures you can perceive: which has the highest current HP, which has the highest Attack Value, and whether any creature is acting under hidden objectives or special instructions this encounter. This requires no action and costs nothing. It is not analysis. It is perception. You simply see what others miss.

Additionally, you have Advantage on all checks to detect hidden, concealed, or invisible creatures, and on all checks to identify ambushes, traps, or environmental threats before they trigger.

**Reactive Awareness** — Level 1 · Core Feature

You have Advantage on all Initiative rolls. You cannot be surprised while conscious.

Once per encounter, when an enemy within Short range attacks an ally or moves in a way you can perceive, you may use your Reaction to do one of the following: move up to your full speed toward that creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks, or make one attack against that creature. This attack is not made at Disadvantage.

**Threat Lock** — Level 3 · Secondary Feature

As a Bonus Action, designate one creature you can perceive as your Threat Lock target. Until the start of your next Turn or until that target is reduced to 0 HP, whichever comes first: you have Advantage on all attack rolls against that target; you know that target's exact position even if they become Hidden or take Total Cover; and the first time that target attacks anyone other than you before the start of your next Turn you may use your Reaction to immediately move up to your full speed toward that target without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

You may only have one Threat Lock target at a time. Designating a new target ends the previous lock immediately. Threat Lock does not refresh automatically — you must spend your Bonus Action again at the start of each Turn to maintain it on the same target or designate a new one.

**Decisive Strike** — Level 5 · Major Feature

Once per encounter, as your Action, make one attack against your current Threat Lock target. If this attack hits, deal maximum damage on all dice. Then roll 1d20 \+ PER \+ Prowess against that target's static DEX Save Value. On a Strong Success, the target is Prone and Slowed until the end of its next Turn. On a normal Success, the target is Slowed until the end of its next Turn. On a failure, nothing happens. If the attack misses, nothing happens.

Note on Setup

Decisive Strike does not require Threat Lock to have been active for a specific duration. The Sentinel may designate a Threat Lock target and use Decisive Strike on the same Turn if they have both a Bonus Action and an Action available. The setup requirement exists in practice because Threat Lock's Advantage on attacks significantly improves the Decisive Strike hit rate.

**Read the Room** — Level 7 · Major Feature

At the start of each of your Turns, without any action required, you immediately know the current HP status (above half, below half, or critical) and the number of remaining Encounter Power uses of every creature you can perceive.

Once per Turn, when you hit a creature that is below half its maximum HP with an attack or Power, you may spend your Bonus Action to impose one of the following on that creature: it is Dazed until the end of its next Turn; it is Slowed until the end of its next Turn; or it drops one held item of your choice.

**Overwatch** — Level 10 · Capstone

Once per encounter, as your Action, you declare Overwatch. This Action also consumes your Movement, Bonus Action, and Reaction for this Turn. Until the start of your next Turn, you have **five Reactions** to spend from the following list. Each Reaction may only be spent once per trigger, and each trigger may only receive one Reaction from you:

* Grant one ally you can perceive Advantage on one Active Defense roll against an incoming attack. Declared after the attack is announced, before the defense roll.  
* Move up to your full speed toward any ally you can perceive who is being attacked, or make one attack against their attacker (extended Reactive Awareness — any range, not only Short).  
* Reduce one attacker's Attack Value by 5 against one ally you can perceive. Declared after the attack is announced, before the ally's Active Defense roll. Cannot combine with the Advantage Reaction on the same attack.  
* Allow one ally you can perceive to immediately move up to half their speed as a free action when targeted by an attack. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.  
* Grant one ally you can perceive Advantage on their next save before the end of that Turn. Declared when the save is triggered.

Unused Reactions from Overwatch are lost at the start of your next Turn.

### Strategist

| Primary | Hit Die | Saves | Effect Value | Rec. Mod. |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Intelligence | d8 | INT, PER | 10 \+ INT \+ PRO | \+0 |

Strategists win by knowing more than the enemy. Not through brute force, not through speed, not through endurance: through understanding. They study the battlefield before the first punch lands, identify vulnerabilities before anyone else has finished drawing breath, and spend every moment of a fight converting information into advantage for themselves and the people beside them.

Some Strategists are detectives who read a crime scene the way others read a book. Others are inventors, battlefield coordinators, criminal architects, scientists who treat conflict as a systems problem, or tactical geniuses who have never lost because they have never gone into a situation without a plan for the situation after this one. What they share is the refusal to be surprised. Every setback was anticipated. Every crisis has a prepared response.

The Strategist is the class that makes everyone around them better by being exactly the right person in exactly the right position at exactly the right time. That is not an accident. It never is.

**Tactical Analysis** — Level 1 · Core Feature

As a Bonus Action, choose one creature you can perceive. You immediately learn one of the following about that creature, chosen by the GM based on what is most tactically relevant: a damage type it has Resistance to; a damage type it is vulnerable to; a Condition it is currently immune to; its current HP relative to its maximum (above half, below half, or critical); or its primary tactical behavior this encounter (aggressive, defensive, evasive, or supporting).

A creature you have analyzed is marked for the rest of the encounter. You may have a number of creatures analyzed simultaneously equal to your INT. Analyzing a new creature beyond that limit removes the oldest mark.

**Tactical Exploitation** — Level 1 · Core Feature

Once per Turn, after you hit with an attack or Power against an analyzed target, or after you succeed on an Investigation, Insight, or Technology check against an analyzed target, choose one of the following effects to apply to yourself or to one ally within Medium range who can perceive you:

* Gain or grant Advantage on the next attack roll against that target before the end of your next Turn.  
* Add your Prowess to the damage of this hit, or grant a chosen ally a bonus equal to your Prowess on their next damage roll against that target before the end of your next Turn.  
* Gain or grant Advantage on the next save forced by that target before the end of your next Turn.  
* Gain or grant temporary HP equal to your INT plus your Prowess.

This feature requires no additional action beyond the attack or check that triggers it.

**Contingency Planning** — Level 3 · Secondary Feature

Once per encounter, when any triggering event occurs during the encounter, you may use your Reaction to declare that you prepared for this. Choose one of the following effects and apply it immediately:

* **Stabilize an ally.** One ally you can perceive who is at 0 HP immediately stabilizes and regains HP equal to your INT plus your Prowess. They are no longer unconscious.  
* **Collapse a position.** Roll 1d20 \+ INT \+ Prowess against one analyzed enemy's INT Save Value. On a success, they lose their next Action as their tactical position falls apart.  
* **Open a route.** One ally you can perceive may immediately move up to their full speed as a free action without provoking Opportunity Attacks.  
* **Clear a condition.** You immediately remove one Condition from yourself or one ally you can perceive.  
* **Enable recovery.** One ally you can perceive may immediately spend one Hit Die as a free action outside of their Turn.

**Calculated Pressure** — Level 5 · Major Feature

Once per encounter, as your Action, choose one analyzed creature you can perceive. Roll 1d20 \+ INT \+ Prowess against that creature's INT Save Value. On a success, until the start of your next Turn the creature's Attack Value is reduced by 3, it cannot use Encounter or Daily Powers, and all attacks against it are made with Advantage. On a failure, nothing happens.

**Expose the Pattern** — Level 7 · Major Feature

Once per Turn, when you hit an analyzed target with an attack or Power, you may spend your Bonus Action to expose their pattern. Until the start of your next Turn, the target loses any Resistance to the damage type of that hit, and every ally who attacks that target before the start of your next Turn adds your INT to their damage roll on a hit.

**Master Plan** — Level 10 · Capstone

Once per encounter, trigger Master Plan in one of two ways:

* **As a Reaction,** when any triggering event occurs, you immediately apply one effect from the Master Plan list.  
* **As a Full Round Action,** you spend your entire Turn in focused tactical execution — no movement, Action, or Bonus Action. At the end of your Turn, apply one effect from the Master Plan list.

Both modes draw from the same once per encounter resource. The Master Plan list:

* **Contingency Executed.** Every ally you can perceive immediately regains one spent Encounter Power of their choice. Cannot refresh Daily Powers.  
* **Systemic Collapse.** Roll 1d20 \+ INT \+ Prowess once and compare against every analyzed enemy's INT Save Value individually. Any enemy whose Save Value your roll meets or beats is Stunned until the end of their next Turn. Any enemy whose Save Value your roll falls short of is unaffected.  
* **Prepared Egress.** Every ally you can perceive may immediately move up to their full speed as a free action without provoking Opportunity Attacks.  
* **Structural Compromise.** Choose one analyzed enemy. Roll 1d20 \+ INT \+ Prowess against the target's static CON Save Value. Success: The target's current Hit Points are reduced by half (rounded down, minimum 1 HP remaining). Failure: nothing happens.  
* **Countermeasures Active.** Every ally you can perceive immediately ends one Condition of their choice currently affecting them.

### Striker

| Primary | Hit Die | Saves | Effect Value | Rec. Mod. |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Fighting | d8 | FIG, DEX | 10 \+ FIG \+ PRO | \+0 |

Strikers believe combat is an art. Not brute force, not speed, not endurance: art. The disciplined application of technique at exactly the right moment, against exactly the right target, through exactly the right gap in their defense. A Striker does not need to hit harder than the Bruiser or move faster than the Vanguard. They need to hit smarter than everyone.

Some Strikers are martial artists who have spent their entire lives reducing conflict to a single perfect technique. Others are gunfighters, assassins, swordsmen, tactical brawlers, or combat veterans who have survived by understanding the difference between fighting and winning. What they share is this: they study every fight before they finish it.

The Striker excels at identifying vulnerability, creating openings where none exist, and cashing in on the conditions they have spent the encounter building. Enemies who underestimate a Striker in the early rounds often cannot respond to them in the later ones.

**Focused Fighter** — Level 1 · Core Feature

At the start of each of your Turns, choose Offense or Defense. It lasts until the start of your next Turn:

* **Offense.** Add your FIG modifier to your damage roll when you hit with an attack or Power that deals damage (all attack types, all damage forms).
* **Defense.** Add your FIG modifier to your Parry/Block Active Defense a second time (1d20 + FIG + FIG + PER + Prowess). Engaging you in melee is a trap.

You gain only one at a time. For **1 Edge**, you may switch as a Reaction (for example, to Defense the instant an attack is declared against you).

**Exploit Opening** — Level 1 · Core Feature

Once per Turn, when you hit with an attack or Power that deals damage against a target that is suffering a Condition, has already taken damage this Turn from any source, or is granting you Advantage, you may spend your Bonus Action to exploit the opening. Roll an additional Power Die and add it to the damage of that hit. Roll 1d20 \+ FIG \+ Prowess against the target's Save Value for the relevant Attribute — DEX if the target was caught off-balance, STR if they were physically compromised, WIS if they were distracted or mentally pressured. On a success, the target is Dazed until the end of their next Turn.

**Combat Read** — Level 3 · Secondary Feature

At the start of each of your Turns, choose one creature you can perceive. This requires no action. Until the start of your next Turn, you know whether that creature has Resistance to any damage type, whether it is currently suffering any Condition, and whether its current HP is above or below half its maximum.

If you spend your Bonus Action before making your first attack this Turn, that attack against the chosen creature is made with Advantage.

**Vital Strike** — Level 5 · Major Feature

Once per encounter, when you hit with an attack or Power that deals damage against a target currently suffering two or more Conditions, you may spend your Bonus Action to declare Vital Strike. Deal maximum damage on all dice for that hit. If the target is reduced to 0 HP by Vital Strike, you may immediately make one additional attack against a different target within Close range as a free action. This additional attack is made at Disadvantage per the secondary attacks rule.

**Killer Instinct** — Level 7 · Major Feature

You always know when any creature you can perceive is below half its maximum HP, without needing to use Combat Read. Against any creature below half HP: your attacks deal additional damage equal to your Prowess; your Exploit Opening Daze roll gains a \+2 bonus; and any critical hit on an attack roll triggers a roll of 1d20 \+ FIG \+ Prowess against the target's CON Save Value — on a success, the target is Stunned until the end of their next Turn.

**Flawless Execution** — Level 10 · Capstone

Once per encounter, as your Action, execute a Flawless Execution strike. Make one attack roll using 1d20 \+ FIG \+ Prowess against the highest Defense Value among all creatures within Close range.

* **If the attack hits:** the primary target takes full damage from the strike; every other creature within Close range takes half that damage; and roll 1d20 \+ FIG \+ Prowess once against every creature in the area's Save Value for the chosen Attribute — STR, DEX, or WIS, declared at the moment of declaration. Any creature whose Save Value your roll meets or beats is both Dazed and Prone until the end of their next Turn. Any creature whose Save Value your roll falls short of is unaffected.  
* **If the attack misses,** nothing happens.

### Vanguard

| Primary | Hit Die | Saves | Effect Value | Rec. Mod. |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Dexterity | d8 | DEX, PER | 10 \+ DEX \+ PRO | \+0 |

Vanguards survive by never being where the attack lands. Their method is motion: constant repositioning, exploitation of momentum, and the discipline to turn movement itself into a weapon. An acrobatic Vanguard flows through combat like water around stone. A teleporter Vanguard is never where you left them. A speedster Vanguard hits and is gone before the pain registers. What unites them is that they control the geometry of every fight they enter.

The Vanguard does not win by enduring. They win by making the enemy swing at empty air.

**Fluid Motion** — Level 1 · Core Feature

Standing from Prone costs you no movement. Climbing and difficult terrain cost you no additional movement. You have Advantage on checks and saves to escape grapples, restraints, and forced movement effects.

When you move at least 15 feet before making an attack, that attack roll is made with Advantage. This Advantage is lost if you are Prone, Restrained, or Immobilized at the time of the attack.

**Evasive Strike** — Level 1 · Core Feature

Once per Turn, when you hit with an attack or Power that deals damage, you may spend your Bonus Action to move up to 15 feet immediately. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

**Momentum Shift** — Level 3 · Secondary Feature

When you take damage from an attack, you may use your Reaction to move up to your full speed immediately. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. If you end this movement at least 15 feet from where you started, your next attack roll before the end of your next Turn is made with Advantage.

**Blitz** — Level 5 · Major Feature

Once per encounter, as your Action, you move up to twice your speed in a straight line. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks and you may choose to stop at any point. Make one attack roll (1d20 \+ DEX \+ Prowess) and compare it to the Dodge Defense Value of every creature whose space you pass through. On a hit, the creature takes one Power Die plus your DEX modifier and is knocked Prone. On a Strong Success, it is also pushed one Zone in the direction of your movement.

**Untouchable** — Level 7 · Major Feature

When you are targeted by an attack you can perceive, you may use your Reaction to gain Advantage on your Active Defense roll against it. If the attack hits, you take half damage instead of full. If the attack misses, you may spend your Bonus Action before the start of your next Turn to move up to 15 feet immediately. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

**Apex Predator** — Level 10 · Capstone

You have Advantage on all attack rolls against any creature that has not yet acted this encounter, or any creature that is currently Prone, Restrained, or Dazed.

When you score a Strong Success on an attack roll, you may use your Reaction to move up to 15 feet immediately. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

Once per encounter at the start of your Turn, you may declare one creature you can perceive as your Target. Until the start of your next Turn, you have Advantage on all attacks against that creature, and you have Advantage on Active Defense rolls against that creature's attacks. This declaration requires no action.

### Warden

| Primary | Hit Die | Saves | Effect Value | Rec. Mod. |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Wisdom | d8 | WIS, CON | 10 \+ WIS \+ PRO | \+2 |

Wardens master themselves first. Inner strength, spiritual resilience, emotional discipline, instinct, composure, and mental endurance define them. They are not nature guardians. They are not mystics by default. They are not healers. They are the heroes who have looked inward, found something unbreakable, and learned to carry that stillness into the worst moments a fight can produce.

A Warden does not need calm surroundings. They bring the calm with them. When everything around them is chaos, fear, manipulation, and psychological pressure, the Warden is the eye of the storm. When an enemy tries to break them through terror, domination, or corruption, the Warden turns that attempt back as a demonstration of exactly how badly the enemy has misjudged the situation.

At their peak, a Warden does not simply resist psychological attack. They make it dangerous to try.

**Inner Fortress** — Level 1 · Core Feature

You have Advantage on all saves against Shaken, Frightened, Dazed, and Charmed. Once per encounter, when you fail any save, you may use your Reaction to reroll it. You must use the new result.

When you use Steady On or Second Wind, you gain temporary HP equal to your WIS in addition to any other effect those actions produce.

**Force of Will** — Level 1 · Core Feature

Once per Turn, when a creature you can perceive targets you or an ally with an effect that would cause Shaken, Frightened, Dazed, or Charmed — whether that effect succeeds or fails — you may spend your Bonus Action to project your discipline outward against that creature. Roll 1d20 \+ WIS \+ Prowess against that creature's WIS Save Value. On a success, the creature is Shaken until the end of its next Turn and immediately loses any ongoing fear or charm effect it is currently sustaining. On a failure, nothing happens.

**Unshakable Ground** — Level 3 · Secondary Feature

You cannot be surprised while conscious. When an encounter begins and you have not yet acted, you may still use your Reaction normally before your first Turn.

Once per encounter, when an ally within Short range fails a save against Shaken, Frightened, Dazed, or Charmed, you may use your Reaction to allow them to reroll that save immediately. They must use the new result.

**Eye of the Storm** — Level 5 · Major Feature

Once per encounter, as a Bonus Action, you declare yourself the eye of the storm. For a number of Rounds equal to your Prowess, you and every ally within Short range are immune to the Shaken, Frightened, Dazed, and Charmed conditions. Any ally who enters Short range of you during this duration immediately gains the immunity for its remaining duration. Any ally who leaves Short range loses it immediately.

**Turning the Tide** — Level 7 · Major Feature

When you succeed on a save against Shaken, Frightened, Dazed, or Charmed, you may spend your Bonus Action to turn that effect back against its source. Roll 1d20 \+ WIS \+ Prowess against that creature's WIS Save Value. On a success, the creature suffers the same Condition it attempted to impose on you, lasting until the end of its next Turn. On a failure, nothing happens.

Additionally, Force of Will no longer requires the triggering effect to have targeted you or an ally this Turn. You may use it against any creature you can perceive as a Bonus Action, once per Turn.

**Transcendent Presence** — Level 10 · Capstone

Once per encounter at the start of your Turn, as a free action, you may declare Transcendent Presence. The following occurs simultaneously:

Roll 1d20 \+ WIS \+ Prowess once and compare against every non-ally creature within Short range's WIS Save Value individually. Any creature whose Save Value your roll meets or beats is Frightened of you until the end of their next Turn and loses all ongoing fear, charm, and mental effects it is currently sustaining. Any creature whose Save Value your roll falls short of is unaffected.

Every ally within Short range immediately ends one Condition of their choice currently affecting them.

For the rest of the encounter, your Eye of the Storm aura is always active regardless of whether your per-encounter use of Eye of the Storm has already been spent. Allies within Short range of you have Advantage on saves against Shaken, Frightened, Dazed, and Charmed for the remainder of the encounter.

## Multiclassing

A hero is defined by how they respond when the pressure hits. Most heroes respond one way — with force, with speed, with will, with presence. That response is their Class, and ten levels of that Class is the fullest expression of who they are.

Some heroes respond in more than one way. A Bruiser who has also learned to absorb punishment like a Guardian. A Vanguard who has trained under a Striker and blends motion with combat mastery. A Beacon who spent years working alongside a Warden and carries some of that discipline into the field. These heroes are multiclassed — they have developed a second method without abandoning the first.

Multiclassing is a choice, not a default. The system supports it, but it is not assumed.

### The Primary Class

Every multiclassed hero has one **Primary Class** — the class with the most levels. In the event of a tie, the Primary Class is whichever class the hero designated first at character creation. The Primary Class cannot be changed once designated.

### Requirements

To multiclass into a Class, a hero must have an Ability Score of 13 or higher in that Class's Primary Attribute. This requirement must be met before the first level in the new Class is taken and must remain met to continue advancing in it.

| Class | Primary Attribute | Required Score |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Beacon | Charisma | 13+ |
| Bruiser | Strength | 13+ |
| Guardian | Constitution | 13+ |
| Sentinel | Perception | 13+ |
| Strategist | Intelligence | 13+ |
| Striker | Fighting | 13+ |
| Vanguard | Dexterity | 13+ |
| Warden | Wisdom | 13+ |

### The Rules

* Total character level never exceeds 10\.  
* Only the Primary Class may exceed Level 5\. Every secondary class is capped at Level 5\.  
* The recommended default is two classes. Three or more are permitted with GM approval, but each additional class adds complexity and dilutes the depth of every class involved.  
* There is no hard limit on the number of secondary classes, provided the GM approves and the hero meets the Ability Score requirement for each.

### Hit Points

A multiclassed hero uses the Hit Die of each class for the levels taken in that class. The die does not flatten to a single type across all levels.

* **Level 1** always uses the standard Starting HP formula with the Primary Class's Hit Die: (full Constitution score \+ Hit Die maximum) × Campaign Rank multiplier \+ Prowess.  
* **Each subsequent level** uses the median of that level's class Hit Die, plus CON (the modifier), plus your current Prowess.

| Class | Hit Die |
| :---- | :---- |
| Guardian | d12 |
| Bruiser | d10 |
| All other classes | d8 |

Worked Example

#### Ex Astris — Bruiser 2 / Striker 2 / Guardian 1 (Street Level)

| Level | Class | Calculation | HP Gained |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| L1 | Bruiser | (Constitution 16 \+ d10 max 10) × 1 \+ PRO 2 | 28 |
| L2 | Bruiser | d10 median (5) \+ CON (+3) \+ PRO (+2) | 10 |
| L3 | Striker | d8 median (4) \+ CON (+3) \+ PRO (+2) | 9 |
| L4 | Striker | d8 median (4) \+ CON (+3) \+ PRO (+3) | 10 |
| L5 | Guardian | d12 median (6) \+ CON (+3) \+ PRO (+3) | 12 |

### Hit Dice Pool — Recovery

A multiclassed character's Hit Dice pool is composed of all their class Hit Dice across every level taken. The player chooses which die to spend from their available pool each time they recover. Spent dice do not return until a full Downtime rest.

* **Second Wind** — Once per encounter, as a Bonus Action. Spend one Hit Die of your choice from your pool and resolve it as normal. One die only. Available mid-fight. See Chapter 14 for the full effect, which also ends one condition and grants Advantage on your next save.  
* **Breather** — Between encounters. Spend as many Hit Dice as you choose from your pool, rolling each one individually and adding CON to each roll.

Both Second Wind and Breather draw from the same pool. Ex Astris's pool: 2d10 (Bruiser levels) \+ 2d8 (Striker levels) \+ 1d12 (Guardian level). Mid-fight Second Wind: might spend the d12 if critically low. Post-encounter Breather: might spend both d10s and the d12, accepting that only d8s remain until Downtime.

### Effect Values in Multiclassing

A multiclassed character has one Effect Value per class in their build, each derived permanently from that class's Primary Attribute. The GM determines which applies based solely on the source of the effect — no class tracking required beyond knowing what produced it.

### Class Features

A hero gains class features only from levels actually taken in that class. Taking one level of Striker gives you the Level 1 Striker core features — nothing from Levels 3, 5, 7, or 10 unless you invest those levels. Class features are gated by level within that specific class, regardless of total character level. A Striker 2 does not have access to Striker Level 3 features even if their total character level is 5\.

Save Training comes from each class as those levels are taken. A hero with Bruiser and Beacon levels is trained in STR, CON, CHA, and WIS saves.

Each class in the build carries its own Class Effect Value. The source of the effect determines which applies.

### The Cost of Breadth

Multiclassing costs exactly one thing: the capstone.

A hero whose Primary Class never reaches Level 10 does not receive that class's capstone feature. The capstone is the reward for dedication — the fullest expression of a hero who committed everything to one way of being under pressure. A hero who chose breadth chose it knowingly.

Design Note

#### A Trade, Not a Penalty

This is not a penalty. It is a trade. Breadth for depth. Range for the peak. Both are valid expressions of who a hero is. Make the choice with open eyes.

A pure Level 10 Striker has Flawless Execution and the ceiling that comes with it. A Level 7 Striker / Level 3 Beacon has neither Flawless Execution nor Rally Cry at Level 5 — but they have something no pure-class hero has: two methods, two identities, two ways to change the shape of a fight.

### Power Picks and Advancement

Power growth is based on total character level, not individual class level. A multiclassed hero gains Power Picks on the same schedule as any other hero. Power Picks may be spent on any Power Set the hero qualifies for, regardless of which class those levels belong to.

All other advancement — Talents, ASI Picks, Skill Picks — follows the standard Advancement Table based on total character level.

## Beyond Level 10

Level 10 is the ceiling. It does not have to be the end.

For campaigns that continue past Level 10 — heroes who have reached their peak and keep showing up anyway — HEROIC 5e provides a framework for continued growth that respects the ceiling while rewarding the players who earned it.

### Legacy Advances

After reaching Level 10, a hero earns one Legacy Advance every ten sessions of play. A Legacy Advance represents the kind of growth that comes not from raw power climbing but from experience, reflection, and time — the things that happen to a hero after they have become who they are.

At each Legacy Advance, choose one of the following:

Legacy Advance Options

* **Deepen.** Gain one Power Pick. This pick may be spent on Enhancements or Branch Powers within Power Sets the hero already possesses. It may not be used to purchase a new Power Set or a new Core Track entry.  
* **Grow.** Gain one Talent from any Talent list the hero qualifies for.  
* **Reach.** Gain the next class feature you do not yet possess in any class you have levels in, taken in level order (Level 1 → 3 → 5 → 7). Alternatively, a hero may begin a new class by taking its Level 1 features — provided they meet that class's Ability Score requirement — and may continue climbing that class one feature at a time with subsequent Reach advances, in level order.

*Example:* A Level 7 Striker / Level 3 Beacon already holds every Striker feature below the capstone. Reach lets them take the Level 5 Beacon feature, Rally Cry, or begin a third class at its Level 1 features.

Important — What the Capstone Costs

The capstone is never available through Reach. A hero who did not reach Level 10 in a class during their primary advancement cannot acquire that class's capstone as a Legacy Advance. The capstone remains the exclusive reward for a hero who committed fully.

### What Legacy Advances Are Not

Legacy Advances do not increase HP. They do not increase Prowess. They do not improve Save Training or Class Effect Value. They are purely horizontal — breadth, depth, and expression, never raw power escalation.

The ceiling stays at 10\. What grows is everything around it.

# **Chapter Seven · Talents**

Talents

Trained edges. Signature techniques. Hard-earned instincts. The heroic layer that makes one hero play differently from another with the same class and powers.

Forty-Nine Talents

* Actor  
* Alert  
* Appeal  
* Athlete  
* Battlefield Leader  
* Cold Reader  
* Counterguard  
* Defensive Fighter  
* Durable  
* Fast Draw  
* Field Commander  
* Forensic Expert  
* Grappler  
* Hard to Kill  
* Improvised Fighter  
* Innovative  
* Inspiring Leader  
* Interrogator  
* Iron Will  
* Jack of All Trades  
* Linguist  
* Lucky  
* Martial Artist  
* Marksman  
* Master of Combat  
* Master Negotiator  
* Mobile  
* Never Give Up  
* Observant  
* Pain Tolerance  
* Pattern Recognition  
* Performer  
* Power Control  
* Power Focus  
* Power Striker  
* Provocateur  
* Psychic Discipline  
* Resilient  
* Sharpshooter  
* Skilled  
* Specialist  
* Surveillance Specialist  
* Takedown Artist  
* Team Player  
* Tireless  
* Tough  
* Underwater Combatant  
* War Caster  
* Weapon Specialist

Talents are HEROIC 5e's replacement for Feats. They are not simply Feats renamed. They are a distinct design layer: trained edges, signature techniques, hard-earned instincts, and operational habits that make one hero play differently from another hero with the same class and powers.

HEROIC 5e separates character identity into clean layers. Origin explains where the hero comes from. Class explains how the hero responds under pressure. Powers define what the hero can do superhumanly. Skills define learned competency. Merits and Flaws define story-facing truths, complications, resources, obligations, and social realities. **Talents sit between Skills and Class features as heroic edges that shape moment-to-moment play.**

The Separation That Keeps Everything Fast

A Talent should never grant a superpower, replace a Skill, or function as a disguised Merit. Flight is a Power. Fame is a Merit. Acrobatics is a Skill. **Athlete is a Talent.** That separation keeps HEROIC 5e fast, readable, and modular.

## What Talents Do

Talents answer one question: what has this hero learned to do better, faster, cleaner, or under greater pressure than most people?

A Talent may represent training, instinct, experience, discipline, combat style, professional mastery, battlefield habit, or heroic nerve. It should feel useful at the table without becoming a new subsystem. Talents provide one or two of the following:

* A narrow but meaningful use of Advantage  
* A new Reaction or Bonus Action option  
* A way to reduce friction in action scenes  
* A specific combat or noncombat trick  
* A situational reroll  
* A minor defensive edge  
* A way to use a Skill under pressure  
* A simple enhancement to teamwork, movement, recovery, or battlefield interaction

Talents avoid large stacking bonuses, Power Dice scaling, resource pools, or feat chains. Clear action types, short triggers, Prowess, Advantage and Disadvantage, minimal bookkeeping.

## What Talents Do Not Do

* **A Talent does not grant a Power.** If an option lets the hero fly, read minds, regenerate, shoot energy, turn invisible, grow to giant size, or breathe in space, it belongs in a Power Tree.  
* **A Talent does not replace a Skill.** If an option simply says "you are good at Technology," that is Skill training, Expertise, or a Specialty.  
* **A Talent does not replace a Merit.** Wealth, fame, secret identity, contacts, legal authority, enemies, obligations, headquarters, and public reputation belong to Merits and Flaws.  
* **A Talent does not replace Class identity.** A Talent can help a hero feel more mobile, tactical, resilient, or inspiring, but it should not outperform a class in their own core lane.

## When Talents Are Gained

Characters gain Talents at Levels 3 and 9\. Origins, campaign rewards, or specific training arcs may grant additional Talents, but the baseline game assumes Talents are special. If every character has six or seven of them, they stop feeling like signature heroic edges.

A Note on Class Overlap

#### Intentional, Not a Bug

Some Talents provide benefits that partially overlap with Class features. This is intentional in two directions. First, a non-Beacon who takes Provocateur gains a meaningful tool the Beacon already has built in. Second, a Beacon who takes Provocateur may use it as a second Bonus Action taunt per Turn since both cost a Bonus Action and the triggers are distinct.

Where a Talent entirely duplicates an existing class feature, it provides its secondary benefit only. These cases are called out directly in the relevant Talent entries.

## Talent Categories

Talents are organized into ten categories, listed for reference only. There are no category restrictions on who can take which Talent.

The Eight Categories

* **Combat:** fighting techniques, weapon mastery, grappling, counters, precision, battlefield pressure.  
* **Mobility:** parkour, rapid movement, escape, controlled falling, vehicle handling, positional tricks.  
* **Resilience:** pain tolerance, recovery, discipline, endurance, resisting fear, staying conscious.  
* **Leadership:** team coordination, rallying allies, battlefield direction, morale support.  
* **Investigation:** detective work, forensic skill, surveillance, pattern recognition, tactical reading.  
* **Technical:** gadget use, hacking under pressure, jury-rigging, vehicle repair, field engineering.  
* **Social:** deception, interrogation, negotiation, performance under pressure, taunts.  
* **Mystic and Mental:** occult discipline, psychic resistance, meditation, trance, mental focus.  
* **General:** broad competencies that do not belong to a single lane.  
* **Power Support:** Talents that refine how a hero uses Power Sets they already have.

## The Talent List

Combat

Counterguard Combat

When a hostile creature within your reach willingly moves away from you, you may make an Opportunity Attack against it even if it Disengages. If you hit, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the current Turn.

This does not stack with class features that already stop movement on a hit; use the stronger effect.

Defensive Fighter Combat

When you take the Evade action, you may also move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Once per encounter, when an attack misses you, you may grant one adjacent ally temporary HP equal to your Prowess.

Fast Draw Combat

You may draw, stow, ready, or switch one weapon or handheld device as part of any attack or Reaction, requiring no separate action. Once per encounter, when Initiative is rolled, you may immediately draw a weapon or device and move up to 10 feet.

Grappler Combat

You have Advantage on checks made to grapple, maintain a grapple, escape a grapple, or shove a creature you are grappling. Once per Turn, when you successfully grapple a target, you may also reduce its Speed by an additional 10 feet until the grapple ends.

Improvised Fighter Combat

You treat improvised weapons as normal weapons for all purposes. Once per Turn, when you hit with an improvised weapon or an environmental attack, choose one: push the target 5 feet; knock over a small object or piece of cover; break fragile terrain or barriers; or impose Shaken on the target until the end of its next Turn.

Marksman Combat

Choose one ranged weapon group: firearms, bows, thrown weapons, or another group with GM approval. Attacks with that group ignore Cover, though not Total Cover. Once per Turn, you may reroll one damage die from a successful attack using that weapon group and take the higher result.

Martial Artist Combat

You add your FIG modifier to unarmed damage in addition to STR, and your unarmed strikes count as Heavy Weapons for damage purposes when both hands are free. Once per Turn, when you hit with an unarmed strike, you may attempt to shove, trip, or disarm the target as a Bonus Action.

Master of Combat (Combat)

You have studied combat in its many forms. Once per encounter, when you make an attack roll, you may reroll one die and use the higher result. Additionally, you gain Advantage on checks made to identify fighting styles, predict an opponent’s next move in combat, or analyze combat techniques.

Sharpshooter Combat

Your ranged attacks ignore Cover, though not Total Cover. Attacking beyond your weapon's stated range band does not impose Disadvantage as long as you can clearly perceive the target. Once per Turn, before making a ranged attack, you may choose to accept Disadvantage on the attack roll. If the attack hits, add one additional Power Die to the damage.

Takedown Artist Combat

When you hit a creature that is Prone, Grappled, Restrained, Dazed, or Shaken, add your Prowess to the damage roll. Once per encounter, when you reduce a target to 0 HP, you may immediately move 10 feet or attempt to shove one adjacent target as a free action.

Underwater Combatant Combat · Mobility

You do not suffer Disadvantage on attack rolls, Athletics checks, or Acrobatics checks due to being underwater. You have Advantage on checks made to swim, fight currents, escape underwater grapples, or maneuver in submerged environments. This Talent does not grant water breathing.

Power Striker Combat

Once per encounter, when you hit with an attack or Power that deals damage, you may add your highest Ability Score modifier to the damage roll a second time. This does not stack with class features that already add the same modifier twice to the same damage roll; use the stronger effect.

Weapon Specialist Combat

Choose one specific weapon or weapon group. Once per Turn, when you hit with that weapon, add your Prowess to the damage roll. This does not stack with class features that already add Prowess to the same damage roll. The bonus applies only once per Turn regardless of how many hits you land.

Mobility

Athlete Mobility

Standing from Prone costs no movement. Climbing costs no additional movement. Once per Turn, when you make an Athletics or Acrobatics check involving running, jumping, climbing, swimming, or controlled movement, you may add your Prowess even if you are not trained. If you are trained, gain Advantage instead.

Mobile Mobility

Your Speed increases by 10 feet. When you move at least 15 feet before making a melee attack or a damaging Power use, the target of that attack cannot make Opportunity Attacks against you until the end of your Turn.

Vanguards: Fluid Motion already provides the Opportunity Attack clause. Vanguards who take Mobile gain only the Speed increase.

Resilience

Durable Resilience

When you spend a Hit Die during a Breather, treat any die roll lower than your CON plus your Prowess as that result instead. Once per encounter, when you would gain the Shaken condition from injury, you may ignore it.

Hard to Kill Resilience

You have Advantage on Grit Saves. Once per day, when you fail a Grit Save, you may treat it as a success instead. If you roll a natural 20 on a Grit Save, you also gain temporary HP equal to your Prowess when you return to consciousness.

Iron Will Resilience

You have Advantage on saves against Frightened, Charmed, Shaken, intimidation, emotional manipulation, and despair effects. Once per encounter, when you fail one of those saves, you may choose to succeed instead, but you become Shaken until the end of your next Turn as a consequence.

Pain Tolerance Resilience

You have Advantage on saves against Dazed, Stunned from physical injury, torture, pain, or shock. Once per encounter, when damage would impose Shaken, Dazed, or knock you Prone, you may ignore one of those effects entirely.

Resilient Resilience

Choose one Ability Score save. You gain training in that save. If you are already trained in it, once per encounter you may reroll a failed save using that Ability Score and take the higher result.

Tireless Resilience

You have Advantage on saves against exhaustion, forced marches, and environmental fatigue, and on Burnout Checks. During a Breather, you may automatically remove the Shaken condition from yourself without spending a resource.

Tough Resilience

Your maximum HP increases by 2 per character Level. This increase applies retroactively to all Levels already gained. Additionally, once per encounter, when you are reduced below half your maximum HP, you gain temporary HP equal to your Prowess.

Leadership

Battlefield Leader Leadership

Once per encounter, when Initiative is rolled, choose a number of allies up to your CHA or INT (whichever is higher) within 60 feet who can perceive you. Each may immediately move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. When an ally follows your spoken tactical direction, they gain Advantage on one check made to carry it out before the end of their next Turn.

Field Commander Leadership

As a Bonus Action, choose one ally within 60 feet who can hear you. That ally may immediately move 10 feet or stand from Prone as a free action. You may use this a number of times per encounter equal to your Prowess, but no ally may benefit more than once per Turn.

Inspiring Leader Leadership

Once per Breather, after speaking to allies for at least one minute, choose a number of creatures up to your CHA plus your Prowess who can hear and understand you. Each gains temporary HP equal to your Level plus your CHA. Additionally, once per encounter as a Bonus Action, you may grant one ally within 60 feet who can hear you temporary HP equal to your Prowess plus your CHA.

Never Give Up Leadership · Resilience

Once per encounter, when an ally within 60 feet who you can perceive would be reduced to 0 HP, you may use your Reaction to allow them to remain at 1 HP instead. That ally gains Shaken until the end of their next Turn.

Team Player Leadership

When you use the Help action for an ally, that ally also gains temporary HP equal to your Prowess. Once per encounter, when an ally within 30 feet misses an attack while benefiting from your Help, they may reroll one damage die or one attack die tied to that action and take the higher result.

Investigation

Alert Investigation · Combat

You have Advantage on Initiative rolls. You cannot be surprised while conscious unless an effect specifically bypasses mundane awareness. You also have Advantage on Notice checks made to detect ambushes, hidden enemies, or imminent danger.

Sentinels: Reactive Awareness already provides Initiative Advantage and surprise immunity. Sentinels who take Alert gain only the Notice check Advantage.

Forensic Expert Investigation

You have Advantage on Investigation and Medicine checks involving crime scenes, physical evidence, wounds, cause of death, ballistic traces, chemical residue, or staged scenes. If you spend at least 10 minutes examining a scene, you may ask the GM one direct question about what most likely happened there.

Observant Investigation

You have Advantage on passive and active Notice and Investigation checks involving small details, hidden clues, concealed objects, surveillance setups, or reading lips. If you can see a creature's mouth and know the language they are speaking, you can understand what they say unless the speech is intentionally obscured or encoded.

Pattern Recognition Investigation

Once per scene, after observing a creature, system, crime scene, battle pattern, or social situation for at least one round, you may make an Investigation, Insight, Notice, Science, or Technology check with Advantage to identify a weakness, repeated behavior, hidden structure, or likely next move.

Surveillance Specialist Investigation · Technical

You have Advantage on Notice and Technology checks involving cameras, sensors, listening devices, stakeouts, tracking signals, or maintaining overwatch. Once per encounter, if you begin combat from a prepared observation position, one ally of your choice gains Advantage on their Initiative roll.

Technical

Innovative Technical

You improvise working solutions from whatever is at hand. You have Advantage on Technology and Science checks made to jury-rig, repair under pressure, or adapt a device to a purpose it was not built for. Once per encounter, you may treat one improvised tool, salvaged component, or scavenged material as though it were exactly the right piece of equipment for the task.

Social

Actor Social

You gain Advantage on Influence and Finesse checks made to impersonate, disguise your voice, mimic behavior, or perform under observation. If you study a person for at least one minute, you may mimic their speech and mannerisms well enough that casual observers have Disadvantage to detect the deception.

Appeal Social

You have a natural magnetism that draws people in. You gain Advantage on Influence checks made to charm, persuade, or attract positive attention. Once per scene, when you succeed on such a check, you may also impose Advantage on one ally’s next social check involving the same target (or group) within the next minute.

Cold Reader Social · Investigation

After speaking with or observing a creature for at least one minute, you gain Advantage on your next Insight, Influence, or Intimidation check against it. If you succeed on that check, you also learn one of the following: the creature's current emotional state, immediate desire, most obvious fear, or the social leverage most likely to affect it.

Interrogator Social

You have Advantage on Intimidation and Insight checks made during interrogation, questioning, or pressure conversations. Once per scene, when a creature lies to you and you succeed on an Insight check against it, you may ask the GM whether the lie is protecting a person, a place, an object, a motive, or a fear.

Master Negotiator Social

You have Advantage on Influence checks made to negotiate, bargain, de-escalate, mediate, or broker terms. Once per scene, if violence has not yet begun, you may force one hostile or tense NPC to pause long enough for one clear sentence or offer, unless they are mindless or already committed to immediate violence.

Performer Social

Choose one performance form: music, oratory, acting, acrobatics, or another with GM approval. You have Advantage on Influence checks using that performance form. Once per scene, when you perform for a crowd, you may shift the crowd's emotional mood one step toward calm, excitement, fear, sympathy, distraction, or awe, provided the situation allows it.

Provocateur Social · Combat

Once per encounter, as a Bonus Action, choose one hostile creature within 60 feet that can hear or understand you. Roll 1d20 \+ CHA \+ Prowess against that creature's static Social Defense Value. On a success, the creature's Attack Value is reduced by 3 against any target other than you before the end of its next Turn.

Beacons: Taunt is strictly stronger and covers the same action economy slot. Beacons who take Provocateur may use it as a second Bonus Action taunt per Turn only when Taunt has already been used that Turn.

General

Jack of All Trades General

When you make a Skill check in which you are not trained, you may add half your Prowess, rounded down. This Talent does not apply to attack rolls or saves.

Linguist General

You learn three additional languages. You have Advantage on checks to decode unfamiliar languages, recognize dialects, identify coded speech, or communicate basic ideas across a language barrier using improvised signals and context.

★ May be selected multiple times — three more languages each time

Lucky General

Once per session, after you roll a d20, you may reroll it and use either result. You may also use this after an attack against you resolves, treating the attacker's Attack Value as 5 lower for that attack.

Skilled General

Gain training in two Skills. Alternatively, gain training in one Skill and one Specialty tied to a Skill you already have.

★ May be selected multiple times — two new Skills (or one Skill and one Specialty) each time

Specialist General

Choose one Skill Specialty. When that Specialty applies, you have Advantage on the check. If you already had Advantage from another source, you may instead add your Prowess to the roll.

★ May be selected multiple times — different Specialty each time

Power Support

Power Control Power Support

Choose one Power Set you possess. Once per encounter, when you would cause collateral damage, lose control, or suffer Disadvantage from unstable use of that Power Set, you may ignore that complication entirely. This Talent never grants new Powers or increases Power Dice.

★ May be selected multiple times — different Power Set each time

Power Focus Power Support

Choose one At-Will Power you possess. Once per encounter, you may gain Advantage on an attack roll with it, or treat one target's relevant Save Value as 5 lower against it.

★ May be selected multiple times — different At-Will Power each time

Mystic & Mental

Psychic Discipline Mystic · Mental

You have Advantage on INT, WIS, and CHA saves against psychic intrusion, mind reading, emotional control, mental domination, and psychic damage effects. Once per encounter, when you succeed on such a save, you may immediately identify the direction or emotional signature of the source if it is within range.

War Caster Mystic · Mental

You have Advantage on saves made to maintain Sustained Powers after taking damage. When a hostile creature provokes an Opportunity Attack from you, you may use a Power instead of a basic attack as that Opportunity Attack, provided the Power's range and action type allow it.

Design Note

#### Building the Skilled Hero, With or Without Powers

Not every hero's edge comes from a Power Set. Some heroes are simply the most trained, most prepared, most knowledgeable person in the room — the detective who reads a scene no one else can, the tactician who has already planned for this, the polymath who always seems to have the one fact that matters. HEROIC 5e supports this hero without inventing a new subsystem for it. Skills, Talents, and Expertise already do the job.

**Skilled** and **Specialist** are both repeatable. Taken at every Talent opportunity (Levels 3 and 9, and later through Legacy Advance's Grow option), they let a hero's trained Skill list grow far past the four picked at creation, with focused Advantage layered on top through Specialties. **Jack of All Trades** covers the gaps between them, so nothing is ever a total blank. **Expertise**, earned through play rather than purchased, is the ceiling — the moment the GM or an Origin recognizes that a hero's dedication to a Skill has become genuine mastery.

**With Powers.** A Strategist with a Power Set (Super Genius, Armor Systems, or otherwise) uses Tactical Analysis and Tactical Exploitation to convert that trained competence into battlefield advantage, while the Power Set supplies the active combat toolkit. This is the tactical genius who is also, mechanically, a genuine threat in a fight — the inventor whose armor makes their intellect a weapon, the founder-scientist who built their own arsenal from first principles.

**Without Powers.** A Trained-Origin hero who takes no Power Set at all still has a full build: Class Features from Strategist or any other Class, a growing wall of Skills and Specialties from repeated Skilled and Specialist picks, and Talents doing the work Powers would otherwise do — Forensic Expert, Cold Reader, Pattern Recognition, Interrogator, and the like. Their Power Picks, if any Origin grants them, can go toward Gear, Contacts, or other Merits rather than a Power Set. This is the hero who wins the fight before it starts, because they were the only one who saw it coming — a master field handler, a detective who has simply never been wrong, someone whose entire arsenal is preparation.

Neither version needs a new Power Set called "Super Skilled." That would spend Power Picks on what Skills, Talents, and Expertise already do — and would blur the line this game deliberately draws between what a hero has *learned* and what a hero can do *superhumanly*.

# **Chapter Eight · Skills**

Skills

Seventeen broad skills. What a hero has practiced, studied, trained in, and developed over time.

This Chapter

* Training & Expertise

* Starting Skills

* Acrobatics  
* Athletics

* Insight  
* Intimidation  
* Investigation

* How It All Stacks

Skills represent learned competency. They are what a hero has practiced, studied, trained in, and developed over time. A hero with high Athletics has put in the work. A hero with Medicine has studied the body and emergency care. A hero with Streetwise has lived in the city long enough to know how it actually operates.

Skills are distinct from Ability Scores, Powers, Talents, and Merits. An Ability Score describes what a person *is*. A Power describes what they can do superhumanly. A Talent describes a signature edge they have developed. A Skill describes what they have *learned*.

Design Note

#### Why Broad Skills

HEROIC 5e uses broad Skills deliberately. Superhero fiction does not function like a medieval trade simulator. A rooftop-prowling vigilante does not need separate skills for rooftop movement, grappling traversal, urban pursuit, evasive tumbling, and acrobatic recovery. Those all fall naturally under Acrobatics. A gadgeteer does not need separate skills for hacking, robotics, electronics, cybernetics, and advanced systems engineering. Those all fall naturally under Technology.

Broad Skills produce faster rulings, easier character creation, cleaner gameplay, and more heroic competence without argument over edge cases. They keep attention on Powers, Talents, battlefield action, and heroic identity rather than spreadsheet-style skill management.

## How Skill Checks Work

When a hero attempts something where training matters and the outcome is uncertain, the GM calls for a Skill check.

1d20 \+ Ability Score modifier \+ Prowess (if trained)

Training means the hero adds their Prowess to the roll. An untrained hero rolls 1d20 \+ Ability Score modifier only.

Each Skill has a default Ability Score that governs its most common uses. The GM may authorize an alternate Ability Score pairing when the fiction supports it. Technology normally uses INT, but a desperate midair power armor repair under extreme physical stress might use Technology with DEX. Athletics normally uses STR, but endurance swimming might use CON. These alternate pairings should reflect genuine fictional logic, not optimization attempts.

## Training and Expertise

A hero's Skill competency has three levels, each building on the last.

Level One

Untrained

Roll 1d20 \+ Ability Score modifier. No Prowess added. A hero can still attempt most tasks — they just lack the practiced edge that training provides.

Level Two

Trained

Roll 1d20 \+ Ability Score modifier \+ Prowess. Standard competency. The hero has put in the work and it shows when it matters.

Level Three

Expertise

Roll 1d20 \+ Ability Score modifier \+ double Prowess. The hero is operating at a level that represents genuine world-class mastery in this domain.

Expertise — Earned, Not Purchased

Expertise may be granted by specific Talents, Origins, or as a campaign reward from the GM when a hero's dedication to a specific Skill has been demonstrated through sustained play. It cannot be purchased during normal advancement. It is earned.

A hero may have Expertise in more than one Skill, but Expertise cannot replace training — training in a Skill is required before Expertise in it can apply.

On the character sheet, record Expertise by writing the Skill name followed by an asterisk: **Investigation**\* or **Technology**\*. The asterisk signals that double Prowess applies.

## Skill Specialties

A Specialty is focused expertise inside a broader Skill. A hero with Technology trained and a Specialty in Power Armor is particularly effective when working on powered armor systems specifically.

When a Specialty directly applies to a check, the hero gains Advantage on that check. If the hero already has Advantage from another source, they may instead add their Prowess to the roll as a bonus on top of Advantage.

Specialties Are Narrow

A Specialty in Power Armor does not apply to standard electronics repair. A Specialty in Forensics does not apply to general Investigation checks. The Specialty applies when the fiction clearly matches — not when a player can construct a plausible argument for it.

On the character sheet, record a Specialty in parentheses after the Skill name: **Athletics (Grappling)** or **Technology (Power Armor)**.

## Starting Skills

At character creation, a hero gains Skill training from two sources. First, they gain the Skill training granted by their Origin. Second, they choose 4 additional Skills from the full list. If a hero would gain training in a Skill they already have, they may instead choose one Specialty tied to that Skill.

## Gaining New Skills

Heroes gain a Skill Pick or Specialty at Levels 2, 5, and 8\. At each of these levels, choose one: gain training in one new Skill, or gain one Specialty tied to a Skill the hero is already trained in.

## Starting Languages

Every hero begins play fluent in one native language, chosen at creation to fit their background. A hero trained in Culture also knows one additional language of their choice, reflecting time spent studying societies and cultures beyond their own.

Fluency is not the same as understanding. A hero fluent in a language through this rule can hold a conversation and read street signs. Whether they understand the customs, history, or politics of the people speaking it is a Culture check, or a Culture Specialty. Fluency is communication. Culture is context.

Some Origins grant an additional language directly as part of their entry. Those are listed under the Origin itself and do not count against this baseline. The **Linguist** Talent adds three further languages per selection, on top of whatever the hero already knows, and may be selected multiple times.

## The Seventeen Skills

The following seventeen Skills cover all areas of heroic competency in modern superhero storytelling.

Acrobatics

DEX

Balance, tumbling, parkour, evasive movement, controlled falls, aerial maneuvering, and physical grace under pressure. Acrobatics covers any situation where the hero needs to move their body with precision, speed, or style. It applies to dodging obstacles, recovering from falls, moving through narrow or unstable spaces, and performing feats of physical coordination.

Athletics

STR

Climbing, swimming, grappling, lifting, jumping, and physical feats of raw power and endurance. Athletics covers any situation where the hero pushes their body against a physical challenge. It applies to scaling walls, resisting forced movement, breaking free of physical restraints, and feats of strength under stress. The GM may pair Athletics with CON for endurance-based applications such as long-distance swimming or sustained effort over time.

Culture

INT

Knowledge of civilizations, societies, history, social customs, subcultures, institutional structures, ideologies, and foreign languages. Culture covers any situation where understanding people at a societal or historical level matters. It applies to identifying the customs of an alien species, understanding the ideology of an enemy organization, navigating unfamiliar institutional hierarchies, and recognizing historical significance. It is not about reading individuals — that belongs to Insight — but about understanding the groups and systems they belong to.

Finesse

DEX

Fine manipulation, concealment, lock techniques, precision handling, and small-scale dexterity under observation or pressure. Finesse covers any situation where the hero needs to do something subtle with their hands. It applies to picking locks, palming objects, concealing items on their person, performing precise manipulation under time pressure, and disabling small mechanical or electronic devices without tools.

Influence

CHA

Persuasion, leadership, negotiation, public speaking, media presence, and emotional appeals to reason or sympathy. Influence covers any situation where the hero tries to change what someone believes, decides, or agrees to through direct appeal. It applies to convincing skeptical officials, rallying frightened civilians, negotiating with criminals, managing public perception, and building trust under pressure.

Insight

WIS

Reading emotions, detecting motives, identifying deception, and understanding psychological states. Insight covers any situation where the hero tries to understand what someone is actually thinking or feeling beneath what they are saying or showing. It applies to detecting lies, reading a room, identifying an NPC's true motivation, and recognizing emotional states that are being concealed.

Intimidation

CHA

Threats, fear projection, coercion, and interrogation through pressure. Intimidation covers any situation where the hero tries to change what someone does through fear rather than persuasion. It applies to threatening criminals into compliance, projecting a terrifying presence, forcing information through psychological pressure, and establishing dominance in a confrontation.

Investigation

INT

Clue analysis, searching, deduction, forensic reasoning, and piecing together what happened from available evidence. Investigation covers any situation where the hero examines a scene, a document, a person's background, or a set of facts and draws conclusions from them. It applies to analyzing crime scenes, researching enemy organizations, searching locations for hidden information, and working out a chain of events from incomplete evidence.

Medicine

INT

Trauma care, diagnosis, emergency stabilization, and understanding of the body and its systems. Medicine covers any situation where the hero assesses or addresses physical injury or illness. It applies to stabilizing a fallen ally, diagnosing an unusual condition, providing emergency care under fire, and understanding biological or chemical threats.

Notice

PER

Awareness, spotting danger, surveillance, overwatch, and trained observational expertise. Notice covers any situation where the hero actively applies their perceptual training to detect something. It applies to spotting hidden enemies, maintaining surveillance on a target, noticing details others miss, identifying ambush setups, and staying alert during extended observation periods.

Occult

WIS

Mysticism, supernatural lore, rituals, dimensional knowledge, spirit understanding, and the traditions and history of the unseen world. Occult covers any situation where knowledge of supernatural forces, entities, or traditions matters. It applies to identifying magical effects, understanding supernatural threats, performing or countering rituals, navigating spirit interaction, and recognizing the significance of occult symbols or events.

Science

INT

Physics, chemistry, biology, engineering theory, mathematics, and the systematic understanding of how the natural world works. Science covers any situation where formal scientific knowledge produces an advantage. It applies to analyzing unknown substances, understanding technological systems at a theoretical level, constructing solutions from first principles, and assessing physical or biological threats.

Stealth

DEX

Sneaking, concealment, infiltration, avoiding detection, and moving or operating without being noticed. Stealth covers any situation where the hero needs to remain unseen, unheard, or generally undetected. It applies to moving through hostile territory, following targets without being spotted, infiltrating guarded locations, and operating in plain sight without drawing attention. A creature attempting to remain undetected is compared against the Vigilance of every hero in the area.

Streetwise

CHA

Criminal culture, gang structures, informant networks, black market access, urban survival, and the unwritten rules of street-level society. Streetwise covers any situation where understanding how the underside of a city operates matters. It applies to finding criminal contacts, navigating gang territories, identifying criminal operations from external signs, accessing illegal goods or services through appropriate channels, and earning the trust of people who do not trust easily.

Survival

WIS

Tracking, navigation, scavenging, environmental endurance, and operating effectively in harsh or wilderness conditions. Survival covers any situation where the hero must function in an environment that is actively hostile to human presence. It applies to tracking targets through natural terrain, navigating without technology, finding food and shelter in the field, identifying environmental hazards before they become threats, and enduring conditions that would break most people.

Technology

INT

Hacking, electronics, repair, cybernetics, advanced systems engineering, and working with complex technological systems. Technology covers any situation where the hero interacts with machines, networks, or electronic systems in a meaningful way. It applies to bypassing security systems, repairing damaged equipment, interfacing with alien or advanced technology, and constructing improvised technological solutions under pressure.

Vehicles

DEX

Driving, piloting, pursuit handling, vehicle combat, and operating any vehicle under ordinary or extreme conditions. Vehicles covers any situation where the hero must control a vehicle effectively. It applies to high-speed chases, combat maneuvers in moving vehicles, pushing vehicles beyond their rated performance, operating unfamiliar vehicle types, and keeping a vehicle functional under damage or stress. The GM may pair Vehicles with FIG for combat-specific maneuvers where combat instinct matters more than physical dexterity.

## Difficulty and Opposed Checks

### Difficulty Classes

The GM sets difficulty using the following standard thresholds. These are starting points — the GM adjusts based on circumstances, available tools, time pressure, and the specific fiction of the moment.

| Task | DC | What It Represents |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Easy | 10 | A trained hero handles this without much effort |
| Standard | 15 | Requires genuine competency to succeed reliably |
| Hard | 20 | At the edge of normal heroic capability |
| Extreme | 25 | Requires exceptional training or favorable conditions |
| Near-Impossible | 30 | Only the best in the world have a realistic chance |

### Opposed Checks

When a hero acts against a resisting NPC, only the hero rolls, against the NPC's relevant static value — a Defense Value, a Save Value, or its Vigilance. Opposed rolls in which both parties roll are used only in the rare case of one player character acting against another, where the higher result wins and ties go to the acting character. Opposed checks use the same formula: 1d20 \+ Ability Score modifier \+ Prowess if trained.

Common Opposed Check Pairings

* **Stealth vs. Notice** — moving without being detected  
* **Influence vs. Insight** — persuasion against a perceptive target  
* **Athletics vs. Athletics** — grappling and physical contests  
* **Finesse vs. Notice** — sleight of hand under observation

### Alternate Attribute Pairings

The GM may allow a Skill to be used with a different Ability Score than its default when the fiction clearly supports it. This is not a player option to optimize with — it is a GM tool to reflect unusual situations accurately. When granting an alternate pairing, the GM states both the Skill and the Attribute before the roll is made.

Common Alternate Pairings

* **Athletics \+ CON** — endurance-based physical effort over time  
* **Vehicles \+ FIG** — combat maneuvers where instinct dominates dexterity  
* **Technology \+ DEX** — delicate physical work under pressure  
* **Intimidation \+ STR** — threat through purely physical presence

## Specialties — Full Reference

The following table lists example Specialties for every Skill. These examples are not exhaustive. A player may propose any Specialty that represents genuine focused expertise within the Skill's scope, subject to GM approval. A Specialty should be narrow enough that it does not simply duplicate the full Skill.

| Skill | Example Specialties |
| :---- | :---- |
| Acrobatics | Aerial Maneuvers, Parkour, Tightrope and Balance, Evasive Movement, Controlled Falls |
| Athletics | Climbing, Swimming, Grappling, Feats of Strength, Endurance Running |
| Culture | Alien Civilizations, Earth History, Criminal Organizations, Religious Traditions, Political Institutions |
| Finesse | Lockpicking, Pickpocketing, Concealment, Safecracking |
| Influence | Public Speaking, Negotiation, Media Relations, Leadership, Diplomacy |
| Insight | Detecting Lies, Reading Crowds, Emotional Assessment, Psychological Profiling |
| Intimidation | Interrogation, Fearsome Presence, Written Threats, Crowd Control |
| Investigation | Forensics, Crime Scene Analysis, Research, Pattern Analysis, Surveillance |
| Medicine | Trauma Surgery, Poison and Toxicology, Field Stabilization, Diagnosis |
| Notice | Ambush Detection, Surveillance, Lip Reading, Tracking by Sound |
| Occult | Demonology, Prophecy, Spirit Communication, Ritual Magic, Dimensional Lore |
| Science | Physics, Chemistry, Genetics, Xenobiology, Engineering Theory |
| Stealth | Urban Infiltration, Wilderness Concealment, Tailing Targets, Silent Movement |
| Streetwise | Gang Culture, Black Market Access, Criminal Contacts, Urban Navigation |
| Survival | Tracking, Wilderness Navigation, Harsh Environment Endurance, Scavenging |
| Technology | Hacking, Power Armor, Security Systems, Cybernetics, Electronics Repair |
| Vehicles | Motorcycles, Jets, Cars and Trucks, Watercraft, Helicopters |

## How Specialties, Training, and Expertise Stack

A hero's Skill competency has three levels — untrained, trained, and Expertise — with Specialties sitting across all three as an additional layer of focused benefit.

Stacking Rules at a Glance

* **Untrained \+ Specialty:** 1d20 \+ Ability Score modifier, with Advantage when the Specialty applies. Prowess is not added. A Specialty does not substitute for training.  
* **Trained \+ Specialty:** 1d20 \+ Ability Score modifier \+ Prowess, with Advantage when the Specialty applies. If the hero already has Advantage from another source, add Prowess as an additional bonus instead.  
* **Expertise \+ Specialty:** 1d20 \+ Ability Score modifier \+ double Prowess, with Advantage when the Specialty applies. Advantage and double Prowess both apply simultaneously — they do not conflict.

The practical summary: Specialties always grant Advantage when they apply. Expertise always replaces single Prowess with double Prowess. These two layers stack cleanly.

Worked Example

A Level 7 hero has Investigation trained, a Forensics Specialty, and Expertise in Investigation. Their Prowess is \+4. Examining a crime scene, they roll 1d20 with Advantage and add \+8 (double Prowess) plus their INT modifier.

Against a DC 20 this is a very reliable success — which is correct. This hero has dedicated themselves to forensic investigation at a level that represents genuine world-class expertise. The math reflects that without requiring a separate subsystem to track it.

# **Chapter Nine · Merits & Flaws**

Merits &  
Flaws

Advantages, obligations, reputations, enemies, resources, and personal story pressure. The part of the character sheet that says who the hero is in the world.

Merits and Flaws are HEROIC 5e's system for character advantages, disadvantages, obligations, social standing, identity complications, resources, relationships, enemies, reputations, and personal story pressure. They are the part of the character sheet that says who the hero is in the world.

A hero is not only a Class, Power Set, Skill list, and Talent selection. A hero may be famous, hunted, wealthy, trusted by the police, cursed, responsible for someone vulnerable, backed by a corporation, despised, or bound by a code. Those things matter in superhero fiction. They deserve rules.

The Separation That Matters

A Merit should not grant a Power. A Flaw should not secretly be a Power Limitation unless it directly affects a Power. A Merit should not replace a Talent. A Flaw should not be a Skill penalty wearing a dramatic hat. Every Merit and Flaw in this chapter has a defined mechanic. If an entry cannot produce a specific die roll, a specific Advantage or Disadvantage, or a bounded once-per-session effect, it does not belong in this system. Merits and Flaws are not story flavor. They are rules with story flavor attached.

## Starting Merits and Flaws

At character creation, each player chooses one of the following starting frameworks.

| Framework | Starting Allowance | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Standard Start | 3 Merit slots & 3 Flaw slots | Recommended default |
| Complicated Hero | 4 Merit slots & 4 Flaw slots | More texture, more pressure |
| Clean Hero | 1 Merit slot & 0 Flaw slots | GM approval required |
| Heavy Drama Start | 5 Merit slots & 5 Flaw slots | GM approval required |

Origin-granted Merits and Flaws do not count against these totals. They are part of the Origin package and are not free player choices. A hero with no Cash Flow, Wealth, or Destitute Flaw is assumed to have a baseline working income: stable but modest, sufficient for ordinary living and standard equipment.

## Merit and Flaw Ratings

Merits and Flaws have Ratings from 1 to 3\. The Rating is also the cost in slots.

| Rating | Cost | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | 1 slot | Minor but meaningful. Fires occasionally. Manageable. |
| 2 | 2 slots | Significant and regularly relevant. Requires active attention. |
| 3 | 3 slots | Major and campaign-shaping. Pervasive across the whole campaign. |

Slot Budget Examples — Standard Start (3 Merit slots, 3 Flaw slots)

* Three Rating 1 Merits — **Legal.** Total cost 3\.  
* One Rating 2 Merit and one Rating 1 Merit — **Legal.** Total cost 3\.  
* One Rating 3 Merit — **Legal.** Total cost 3\.  
* One Rating 3 Merit and one Rating 1 Merit — **Illegal.** Total cost 4\.

## Flaw Effect Values

When a Flaw calls for a save, the Effect Value is fixed by the Flaw's Rating. The player always rolls the save using the relevant Ability Score modifier plus Prowess if trained. The GM never rolls.

| Rating | Effect Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| 1 | 15 |
| 2 | 20 |
| 3 | 25 |

| Situation | Save Attribute |
| :---- | :---- |
| Resisting fear, guilt, temptation, rage, or obsession | WIS |
| Resisting addiction, pain, withdrawal, or physical stress | CON |
| Resisting interrogation, public pressure, or humiliation | CHA |
